input.title: Relax the jiff =0.2.28 pin to ^0.2.46
input.description:
The workspace pins `jiff = "=0.2.28"` (PR #109). Each published crate that uses jiff carries this exact requirement, so core does too. A downstream project that needs a newer jiff cannot use the current core. Cargo then fails to resolve, or it selects an older core.

The pin existed because jiff 0.2.29 pulled `defmt` and the unmaintained `proc-macro-error2` (RUSTSEC-2026-0173). jiff 0.2.46 does not pull either crate. `cargo audit --deny warnings` and `cargo deny check` pass with 0.2.46.

Scope: change the requirement to the caret form `0.2.46` and update `Cargo.lock`. Do not move to jiff 1.0 here. `jiff::Timestamp` is in the public API of core (`SessionEvent`), so jiff 1.0 is a breaking change for core and needs its own issue.

The gates are running. While they run, here is the status.

**Cause.** The `=0.2.28` pin is in the root `[workspace.dependencies]`, so every published crate carries it. Core 0.5.21 on crates.io requires `jiff =0.2.28`. A downstream project that needs a newer jiff cannot use that core, so Cargo fails or selects an older core.

**Why the pin existed.** PR #109 added it because jiff 0.2.29 pulled `defmt` and the unmaintained `proc-macro-error2` (RUSTSEC-2026-0173). I checked jiff 0.2.46. It pulls neither crate, and `cargo audit --deny warnings` and `cargo deny check` both pass.

**Change** (branch `feature/sma-818-relax-the-jiff-0228-pin-to-0246` in a scratchpad worktree, Linear issue SMA-818):
- `Cargo.toml`: the requirement changes from `=0.2.28` to `0.2.46` (a caret range), and the comment now gives the new reason.
- `Cargo.lock`: jiff and jiff-static go to 0.2.46, and jiff adds the new `jiff-core 0.1.8` dependency.

**Why not jiff 1.0.1.** `jiff::Timestamp` is a public field type on core's `SessionEvent`. A move to 1.0 is a breaking change for core and its dependents, so I kept it out of scope. Tell me if you want 1.0 now.

**Not related to jiff:** release PR #345 is red on `clippy` because the `aws_config::BehaviorVersion::v2026_11_10` deprecation fails the bedrock build. PR #347 (SMA-817) is open for that.

I will report the gate results when they finish. After that, I will commit and open the PR if you agree.

The jiff bump to 0.2.46 is ready and checked. Nothing is committed or pushed yet.

**Gate results**
- `cargo fmt --check`, clippy (`-D warnings`), and the docs build (`-D warnings`) pass.
- `cargo audit --deny warnings` and `cargo deny check` pass. jiff 0.2.46 no longer pulls in `proc-macro-error2`, which was the reason for the old pin.
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features`: 498 tests pass and 1 fails. The failure is `trybuild_ui` in core: 5 builder compile-error snapshots do not match. The change does not cause it. The same 5 cases also fail on unchanged `main` with jiff 0.2.28.
- The cause is probably my local toolchain. `stable` here is rustc 1.99.0 (2026-09-28), and all six `test` legs pass on `main` in CI. I did not check which rustc CI uses. You can run `! rustup update stable` to make your local result match CI.

**The change**, on branch `feature/sma-818-relax-the-jiff-0228-pin-to-0246` (Linear SMA-818):
- **`Cargo.toml`:** the jiff requirement changes from `=0.2.28` to `0.2.46`, and the comment now says why an exact pin causes problems.
- **`Cargo.lock`:** jiff and jiff-static move to 0.2.46, and the new `jiff-core 0.1.8` is added.

**Release effect.** Every crate that depends on jiff now publishes a manifest with the relaxed version range. I expect release-plz to give these crates patch bumps and to cascade to the facade. That is the result we want, because the consumer conflict only goes away when core ships again. No hand-bumped versions are necessary.

**Next step.** Do you want me to commit (`chore(deps): SMA-818 relax the jiff pin to ^0.2.46`), push, and open the PR? The worktree is `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-smaschek-dev-paigasus-paigasus-helikon/bf74618b-413e-4123-b1fd-a86f23ea095d/scratchpad/jiff-wt`.
